children: Patanjali Foods shares extended their recent rally on Monday, September 21, rising more than 6 percent after the company's management struck an optimistic note on its FY27 growth prospects, particularly in FMCG and edible oils, while also forecasting strong free cash flow.

The stock climbed 6.5 percent to Rs 390.75 in late-morning trade, taking its four-session gain to about 15 percent. Despite the rebound, Patanjali Foods remains down around 30 percent in 2026 so far, compared with a 10.7 percent decline in the Nifty 50. The company had a market capitalisation of about Rs 42,300 crore.

Sanjeev Asthana, CEO of Patanjali Foods, told CNBC-TV18 that the company expects its FMCG business to grow 18-20 percent in FY27, while the foods business is projected to expand 8-10 percent. Edible oils are expected to register growth of more than 4 percent. Asthana said the company was confident of meeting its FY27 targets and expects to generate free cash flow of Rs 700-800 crore during the year.

The management commentary on consumer demand was more mixed. Asthana said urban demand remained strong and the festive season was expected to be good, but the company was less optimistic about rural demand because of the poor monsoon. Supply conditions in edible oils are another concern. According to Asthana, more than 90 percent of India's sunflower oil imports are currently stuck, making supply a major issue.
Asthana also said there were no regulatory issues concerning the company's foods business and that no loans had been taken against the promoters' 38 percent stake.

The latest management outlook follows a strong June-quarter performance. Patanjali Foods' consolidated net profit surged 86 percent year on year to Rs 335.7 crore in Q1 FY27, while revenue from operations rose 29 percent to Rs 11,337.5 crore. EBITDA increased 69 percent to Rs 543.3 crore, with the EBITDA margin expanding to 4.8 percent from 3.7 percent a year earlier. The June quarter marked the company's fourth consecutive quarter of record revenue.

The stock's recent gains have also coincided with legal relief for the broader Patanjali group after the Delhi High Court quashed seven Income Tax Appellate Tribunal orders concerning Patanjali Ayurved, criticising procedural lapses and the tribunal's handling of the matters.
